title: 5. Leading Operational KPIs, Structural Potential & CEO Walk-the-Talk
subtitle: Six operational indicators that drive earnings and a five-year audit of Munot family capital allocation

web_blocks.html: Because ZF Steering Gear straddles two distinct industrial cycles—commercial-vehicle steering and aluminium/solar-frame manufacturing—headline quarterly revenue alone can mislead an owner. Tracking six leading operational KPIs separates genuine demand momentum from temporary margin or working-capital noise [1][8].

web_blocks.takeaway: Working capital days (21) and top-line momentum (+53% YoY in Q2 FY27) are flashing green, while CWIP buildup (₹103 Cr) and sub-7% ROCE remain the critical watchpoints.

web_blocks.html: Auditing management's 3-to-5-year walk-the-talk record yields a balanced, unvarnished scorecard. On the operational front, the Munot leadership delivered what it promised: it amicably resolved the Bosch overhang via the 2023 buyout [15], consolidated the Supa land lease from NexSteer into DriveSys [13], commissioned commercial aluminium and solar-frame production [12], launched the Metacast Auto foundry in Kolhapur [17]. Cut net working capital from 103 days in FY2022 to 21 days in FY2026 [1].

On the capital-efficiency and minority-shareholder front, however, the execution record is far less flattering. Despite reporting positive net profits in every recent fiscal year, the company paid zero dividends in FY2025 and FY2026 (3-year payout of just 5.54%) [1]. Consolidated ROE slumped to 3.29% (5.21% 3-year average) and ROCE sat at 6.48%, well below domestic cost of capital [1]. Meanwhile, consolidated borrowings climbed nearly fivefold from ₹34 crore in March 2022 to ₹165 crore in September 2026 as CWIP swelled to ₹103 crore [1]. Management has proven it can build factories. It has not yet proven those factories earn double-digit returns on capital.

web_blocks.mechanism: A dominant Indian commercial-vehicle component duopoly supplier (parabolic and tapered leaf springs for Tata Motors and Ashok Leyland) invested in regional plant proximity and backward-integrated machining during a multi-year CV recovery.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: Operating margins expanded from ~9% to ~14%–15% as plant utilization crossed 75%, driving ROCE above 25% at the peak of the 2016–2018 truck cycle before reverting sharply when CV tonnage fell in FY2020.
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: Shows the upside case if ZFSTEERING's Supa and Kolhapur plants reach >75% utilization during a sustained CV upcycle, while reminding owners that CV component margins remain inherently cyclical.

web_blocks.html: The walk-the-talk audit leaves us with one decisive test: can the newly commissioned assets at Supa and Kolhapur lift consolidated returns on capital out of the mid-single digits? In the next chapter, we examine the full 10-year financial statements, cash conversion. Balance sheet to see how much margin for error the numbers actually provide.

Tracking management's walk-the-talk record over the past three years reveals a split scorecard [5, 8]. On execution of physical assets and working-capital compression, management delivered: DriveSys Systems was commissioned at Supa, consolidated quarterly sales scaled from ₹111 Cr in Q2 FY25 to ₹184 Cr in Q2 FY27. Working capital fell from 46 days to 20.6 days [5, 8]. On capital efficiency and shareholder payouts, however, ROCE remains at 6.48% and dividends were suspended to zero in FY25–FY26 [8].

Beyond quarterly sales and OPM, investors should track consolidated Capital Work-in-Progress (CWIP) turnover and interest-coverage trends each half-year [8]. With CWIP at ₹103 Cr in September 2026 and borrowings at ₹165 Cr, the key inflection occurs when quarterly depreciation stabilizes and incremental asset turns exceed 1.5x without requiring fresh term debt [8].

Monitoring capital-allocation discipline requires watching dividend resumption and debt reduction alongside revenue growth [8]. After paying zero dividends in FY25 and FY26 to fund the ₹109 Cr FY26 capex cycle, returning to positive free cash flow and trimming gross borrowings below ₹120 Cr over FY27–FY28 would provide concrete proof that the expansion phase is maturing [8].
In addition, monitoring quarterly promoter shareholding disclosures alongside CWIP capitalization milestones ensures early visibility into any governance or capital-allocation shifts [3, 8].
Quarterly tracking should stay simple and objective. Watch consolidated sales above ₹180 Cr, margins above 12%, and falling CWIP. Together, those three lines confirm real asset turn.

book_paragraphs: If you want to track ZF Steering Gear without getting lost in quarterly noise, keep your eyes on six operational indicators. First is domestic heavy-truck and tractor wholesale growth, which drives core steering volume. Second is utilization at DriveSys's Supa aluminium and solar-frame plant, which generated over ₹214 crore of consolidated revenue delta in FY2026. Third is consolidated operating margin, which needs to climb from 13%–14% toward 15%–16% as new lines absorb fixed costs.

The other three indicators sit on the balance sheet. Fourth is net working capital days, where management deserves real credit for cutting the cycle from 66 days in FY2024 to 21 days in FY2026. Fifth is Capital Work-in-Progress, which jumped to ₹103 crore by September 2026—a sign that heavy construction is still underway and must soon turn into revenue-producing assets. Sixth, and most decisive, is consolidated ROCE, currently sitting at just 6.48%.

When you audit what the Munot management promised versus what it delivered over the last five years, you get two very different report cards. Operationally, they delivered: they bought out Bosch cleanly in 2023, consolidated Supa into DriveSys, started the aluminium and solar-frame lines, launched the Kolhapur foundry, and tightened working capital dramatically. Financially, however, minority owners have waited a long time for a payoff. Three-year ROE averages just 5.21%, dividend payouts dropped to zero in FY2025 and FY2026, and debt rose from ₹34 crore in 2022 to ₹165 crore by September 2026.

Jamna Auto Industries between 2012 and 2020 offers a useful parallel for what good execution looks like in Indian commercial-vehicle components. Like ZF Steering, Jamna held a dominant OEM position in leaf springs and invested in plant proximity; when truck volumes surged, operating margins expanded from 9% to 15% and ROCE jumped above 25% before the next freight downturn pulled it back. That is the upside blueprint for ZF Steering Gear—provided Supa and Kolhapur finish their capex cycle soon. Next, let us open the 10-year financial statements to check every line of cash flow and debt.
Consistent quarterly execution across all five operational KPIs remains the clearest proof that management is converting physical capacity into durable shareholder value.

book_subsections.title: The Five Leading KPIs That Run This Business
paragraphs: If you want to know how ZF Steering Gear's earnings will look six months before they hit the headlines, ignore daily news chatter and track five operational indicators. First is domestic M&HCV production tonnage and tractor wholesale volumes, which still drive the highest-margin standalone revenue.

Second is capacity utilization at DriveSys Systems' 20,000 MTPA aluminium extrusion lines in Supa [5]. Extrusion is a fixed-cost business where crossing 70 percent utilization transforms unit margins. Third is the conversion of the ₹103 Cr Capital Work-in-Progress balance into revenue-generating gross block [8].

Fourth is working-capital days, which management compressed to 20.6 days [8]; any reversal above 45 days would signal channel stuffing or stressed customer receivables. Fifth is gross debt versus operating EBITDA, ensuring borrowings of ₹165 Cr begin stepping down rather than climbing past ₹200 Cr [8].

book_subsections.title: Management Walk-the-Talk: Execution vs. Return on Capital
paragraphs: When we audit management's promises against actual delivery over the last three years, the verdict is mixed but fair. Management promised to diversify away from pure-play truck cyclicality by building an integrated aluminium and solar-frame vertical—and they built it, taking consolidated TTM revenue to ₹645 Cr [5, 8].

Where they have not yet delivered is return on equity and cash return to minority shareholders. With three-year average ROE at 5.21 percent and dividend payout cut to zero in FY25 and FY26, minority investors have funded a multi-year capex cycle without yet seeing the cash-yield payoff [8].

book_subsections.title: What Good Execution Looks Like Over the Next Four Quarters
paragraphs: Let us set clear, objective goalposts for management over the next twelve months so we are never fooled by narrative spin. First, consolidated quarterly sales need to hold in the ₹175–₹200 Cr range rather than slipping back to ₹130 Cr.

Second, operating profit margins must stay at or above 12 percent without relying on one-off treasury gains in Other Income. Third, that ₹103 Cr Capital Work-in-Progress balance needs to start shrinking as projects capitalize and generate cash.
If all three happen together, consolidated ROCE will naturally climb out of the 6 percent cellar toward double digits, proving that the multi-year capex wave was worth the wait.

book_subsections.title: Why Dividend Resumption Will Be a Crucial Signal
paragraphs: When a historically profitable manufacturer suspends its dividend for two straight years—0 percent payout in FY25 and FY26 [8]—minority shareholders rightly ask where the cash went. Here, the forensic trail is clear: management poured ₹109 Cr in FY26 alone into fixed assets and working capital [8].

We do not mind a company retaining earnings when those retained rupees earn 18 to 20 percent return on capital. When consolidated ROCE sits at 6.48 percent, however, every rupee retained has to prove it can earn more than a bank deposit.
Once DriveSys finishes capitalizing its ₹103 Cr CWIP, you and I should look for two signals: gross debt stepping down from ₹165 Cr and the board reinstating a modest cash dividend.

book_subsections.title: Keeping Score Every Quarter
paragraphs: Good fundamental investing is not set-and-forget. Every ninety days when results drop, check three numbers in five minutes: consolidated sales versus ₹180 Cr, operating margin versus 12 percent, and total borrowings versus ₹165 Cr.
If those three lines move in the right direction together, the thesis is on track.

book_subsections.title: Connecting Operational KPIs to Shareholder Returns
paragraphs: Ultimately, operational KPIs only matter if they translate into higher return on capital employed and growing free cash flow per share. Tracking quarterly sales above ₹180 Cr, operating margins above 12 percent, and CWIP conversion below ₹50 Cr gives you an early, objective dashboard [8].
When those operational gears mesh smoothly, earnings growth and balance-sheet deleveraging reinforce each other, creating the conditions for sustainable long-term value creation.

book_subsections.title: Why Quarterly Discipline Prevents Thesis Drift
paragraphs: When a manufacturing company is in the middle of a multi-year capital cycle, quarterly headlines can easily distract you from what matters. A single strong quarter of sales growth feels exciting, yet it means little if working capital swells or borrowing costs climb just as fast.

By anchoring your review on five operational metrics—M&HCV tonnage, DriveSys extrusion utilization, CWIP conversion, working-capital days, and gross debt—you keep the analysis grounded in factory reality rather than management optimism.

book_subsections.title: Separating Real Utilization From Seasonal Noise
paragraphs: Commercial vehicle and tractor demand always fluctuates between monsoon quarters and festive freight peaks. Rather than reacting to a single strong or weak month, compare four-quarter rolling revenue against installed capacity at Shirur and Supa.
When rolling sales rise while Capital Work-in-Progress and gross borrowings both step down, you have clear evidence that the investment phase is finally paying off.
